# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Thorsted_2019_endotoxin")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0211981> (PMC6383944, open access)
* Supplements: S1 Text (the final NONMEM control stream, with every ODE) and
  S1 Table (the 116-piglet modelling dataset), both deposited with the PLOS ONE
  record.

Thorsted 2019 is a semi-mechanistic model of the innate immune response to
intravenously infused endotoxin (ETX, *E. coli* O111:B4) in anaesthetised
piglets. It links three measured time-courses:

* **ETX** follows one-compartment disposition with Michaelis-Menten elimination
  and a constant assay baseline.
* **TNF-alpha** follows a turnover model whose production rate is stimulated by
  a sigmoidal Emax in the ETX concentration.
* **IL-6** follows a turnover model whose production rate is stimulated linearly
  by the relative increase in TNF-alpha and by ETX, with plasma appearance
  delayed through four transit compartments.

Endotoxin tolerance is built in: the ETX concentration raises `EC50` of the
ETX-TNF-alpha relationship through a three-stage moderator chain, so continued
exposure progressively blunts the TNF-alpha response.

## Why two endotoxin compartments

The source `$MODEL` block declares two ETX compartments with identical kinetics
(same `Vmax`, `KM`, `Vc`) that receive the same infusion and differ only in
their initial condition:

* `central` starts at zero. Only this pool drives TNF-alpha and IL-6, because
  (Results, "Host response") control groups showed no cytokine response to the
  constant baseline or to the pre-study contamination.
* `central_contam` starts at a pre-study contaminating amount in the
  contamination mixture sub-population (`MIX_ETX_CONTAM = 1`, Eq 1). The
  measured endotoxin concentration is `Cc = rbase_etx + central_contam / vc`.

Because elimination is Michaelis-Menten, the two pools are not additively
separable, so a single state cannot give both the measured concentration and
the pharmacologically active one. Every dosing record must therefore be given
to **both** compartments; the source dataset does this with two `EVID = 1` rows
(CMT 1 and CMT 2) of the same amount and rate.

This is an endogenous / mechanistic model: there is no classical
absorption-distribution-elimination profile of an administered drug to
integrate (the "drug" is an immune stimulus), so NCA is not the right
validation. Instead the sections below check the biological steady state,
recovery after a perturbation, mass balance at steady state, dimensional
consistency, and reproduction of the paper's Figure 6.

# Population

The model was fit to 116 anaesthetised piglets (approximately 12 weeks old,
mean weight approximately 27 kg) pooled across six studies (A-F; Thorsted 2019
Table 1), contributing 278 ETX, 1068 TNF-alpha and 1045 IL-6 observations. ETX
was infused intravenously for 1-30 h at 0 (saline) to 16.0 ug/kg/h; the batch
potency was 1000 EU/ug (studies A, B, E) or 3000 EU/ug (studies C, D, F). ETX
was measured in studies C, E and F only. A seventh study (G, n = 6) was held out
for external evaluation and is not part of the fit.

```{r population}
mod()$population
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value is traced to its source in an in-file comment next to the
parameter in
`inst/modeldb/pharmacodynamics/Thorsted_2019_endotoxin.R`. The table collects
them. Structure is from S1 Text; final values are from Table 2 (the stream's
`$THETA`/`$OMEGA` blocks are the run045 *initial* estimates, e.g. `KM` 12325.3
vs Table 2's 12600, so Table 2 governs per the standard initial-vs-final rule).

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| `lvmax` | 442000 EU/h | Table 2 `Vmax` |
| `lkm` | 12600 EU/L | Table 2 `KM` |
| `lvc` | 36.1 L | Table 2 `Vc` |
| `lrbase_etx` / `lrbase_etx_f` | 155 / 1810 EU/L | Table 2 `BASE ETX` (Endochrome C+E / Coatest F) |
| `lprop_cont` | 132 | Table 2 `Propcont`; Eq 1 |
| `lmtt_tnf` | 1.04 h | Table 2 `MTT TNF-alpha` |
| `lrbase_tnf` / `_e` / `_cf` / `_d` | 281 / 25.4 / 3.06 / 68.2 ng/L | Table 2 `S0,TNF-alpha` (DuoSet A+B / DuoSet E / BioSource C+F / BioSource D) |
| `lemax_tnf` | 2540 | Table 2 `Emax` |
| `lec50_tnf` | 286 EU/L | Table 2 `EC0` |
| `lhill_tnf` | 2.10 | Table 2 `gamma` |
| `lmtt_tol` | 6.33 h | Table 2 `MTT EC50` |
| `lemax_tol` | 45100 | Table 2 `Tmax` |
| `lec50_tol` | 29300 EU/L | Table 2 `TC50` |
| `lmtt_il6` | 1.45 h | Table 2 `MTT IL-6` |
| `lrbase_il6` / `_cdf` | 49.2 / 8.19 ng/L | Table 2 `S0,IL-6` (DuoSet A+B+E / BioSource C+D+F) |
| `lslope_tnf` | 0.961 | Table 2 `ESLP,TNF-alpha`; Eq 2 |
| `lslope_etx` | 0.00937 | Table 2 `ESLP,ETX` |
| `expSd` / `expSd_tnf` / `expSd_il6` | 0.321 / 0.485 / 0.505 | Table 2 residual error |
| IIV (6 terms + KM-Vc correlation) | see below | Table 2 CV%; r(KM,Vc) = -0.42 |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(central_contam)` | n/a | S1 Text `$DES` (Michaelis-Menten ETX) |
| `d/dt(tnf)` | n/a | S1 Text `$DES`; Eq 3 |
| `d/dt(moderator1..3)` | n/a | S1 Text `$DES` (tolerance chain) |
| `d/dt(transit1..4)`, `d/dt(il6)` | n/a | S1 Text `$DES`; Eq 2 |

**IIV reading.** Table 2 footnote c reports variability "on the approximate
standard deviation scale", and `100 * sqrt(omega^2)` reproduces the printed CV%
column against the stream's `$OMEGA` variances (e.g. `KM`: `100*sqrt(1.44)` =
120, matching the printed 120; the exact log-normal CV would be 180). So the
variances are `omega^2 = (CV/100)^2`, and the KM-Vc covariance is
`-0.42 * 1.20 * 0.753 = -0.3795` (Results reports the correlation as -0.42; the
stream's block gives -0.4251).

## Units table (dimensional check)

| ODE term | Units multiply to | Equals `d/dt(state)` |
|----------|-------------------|----------------------|
| `vmax * (A/vc) / (km + A/vc)` | (EU/h)(EU/L)/(EU/L) = EU/h | EU/h |
| `kin_tnf * (1 + eff_tnf)` | (ng/L / h)(unitless) = ng/L/h | ng/L/h |
| `kout_tnf * tnf` | (1/h)(ng/L) = ng/L/h | ng/L/h |
| `kin_tol * (1 + tol)` | (EU/L / h)(unitless) = EU/L/h | EU/L/h |
| `kout_il6 * transit` | (1/h)(ng/L) = ng/L/h | ng/L/h |
| `slope_etx * cp_etx` | (L/EU)(EU/L) = unitless | n/a (adds to stimulation) |

`eff_il6 = slope_tnf * (tnf/rbase_tnf - 1) + slope_etx * cp_etx` is unitless, as
required of a multiplier on the IL-6 production rate: the TNF-alpha term is a
ratio and `slope_etx` carries L/EU to cancel the EU/L of `cp_etx`.

# Steady-state check

With no infusion the system must sit at its biological baseline indefinitely:
measured ETX at `rbase_etx`, TNF-alpha at `rbase_tnf`, IL-6 at `rbase_il6`, and
`EC50` at `EC0`. Solve the typical-value model (study A/B, no contamination) for
60 h with no dose.

```{r steady-state}
typ <- mod |> rxode2::zeroRe()

cov0 <- list(
  MIX_ETX_CONTAM = 0, STUDY_ETX_C = 0, STUDY_ETX_D = 0,
  STUDY_ETX_E = 0, STUDY_ETX_F = 0
)

# The model has three endpoints (Cc, tnf, il6), so rxode2 only accepts an
# observation row whose `cmt` is one of them. `tnf` is both an endpoint and an
# ODE state, so it is used throughout; rxode2 still returns every state and Cc
# on each row.
obs_rows <- function(times, covs) {
  out <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "tnf")
  for (nm in names(covs)) out[[nm]] <- covs[[nm]]
  out
}

ev_ss <- obs_rows(seq(0, 60, by = 1), cov0)

s_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ, ev_ss, returnType = "data.frame")

# ETX, TNF-alpha, IL-6 and EC50 should hold at the reported baselines.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(s_ss$Cc - 155)) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(s_ss$tnf - 281)) < 1e-4,
  max(abs(s_ss$il6 - 49.2)) < 1e-4,
  max(abs(s_ss$moderator3 - 286)) < 1e-4
)
range(s_ss$tnf)
range(s_ss$il6)
```

In the contamination sub-population the measured ETX must start at the
assay baseline plus the contaminating amount of Eq 1:

```{r contam-init}
cov_c <- cov0
cov_c$MIX_ETX_CONTAM <- 1
ev_c <- obs_rows(seq(0, 6, by = 0.5), cov_c)

s_c <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ, ev_c, returnType = "data.frame")
# central_contam(0) = rbase_etx * prop_cont = 155 * 132 = 20460 EU;
# Cc(0) = rbase_etx + 20460/vc = 155 + 20460/36.1.
stopifnot(abs(s_c$Cc[s_c$time == 0] - (155 + 155 * 132 / 36.1)) < 1e-6)
s_c$Cc[s_c$time == 0]
```

# Perturbation recovery

`rxSolve(inits = )` cannot be used to displace the cytokines, because the model
sets `tnf(0)` and `il6(0)` from their baselines and that assignment takes
precedence. Two perturbations are applied with events instead, and each is
first asserted to have moved the system before its recovery is checked:

* a bolus that doubles TNF-alpha and IL-6 at `t = 0` with no ETX present;
* a 1 h ETX infusion at 4000 EU/kg/h (27 kg piglet) into both ETX pools, which
  stimulates both cytokines and raises EC50 through the tolerance chain.

After the ETX has been eliminated, every state must return to its baseline.

```{r perturb}
obs_grid <- seq(0, 72, by = 0.5)

ev_bolus <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = c(281, 49.2),
             cmt = c("tnf", "il6")),
  obs_rows(obs_grid, list())
)
for (nm in names(cov0)) ev_bolus[[nm]] <- cov0[[nm]]

pulse_rate <- 4000 * 27 # EU/h
ev_pulse <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = pulse_rate, rate = pulse_rate,
             cmt = c("central", "central_contam")),
  obs_rows(obs_grid, list())
)
for (nm in names(cov0)) ev_pulse[[nm]] <- cov0[[nm]]

s_bolus <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ, ev_bolus, returnType = "data.frame")
s_pulse <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ, ev_pulse, returnType = "data.frame")

end_of <- function(s) s[s$time == max(s$time), ]
rel_dev <- function(x, ref) abs(x / ref - 1)

stopifnot(
  # The perturbations happened.
  max(s_bolus$tnf) > 1.5 * 281,
  max(s_bolus$il6) > 1.5 * 49.2,
  max(s_pulse$tnf) > 10 * 281,
  max(s_pulse$il6) > 10 * 49.2,
  max(s_pulse$moderator3) > 10 * 286,
  # ...and every state relaxed back to its baseline by 72 h.
  rel_dev(end_of(s_bolus)$tnf, 281) < 0.01,
  rel_dev(end_of(s_bolus)$il6, 49.2) < 0.01,
  rel_dev(end_of(s_pulse)$tnf, 281) < 0.01,
  rel_dev(end_of(s_pulse)$il6, 49.2) < 0.01,
  rel_dev(end_of(s_pulse)$moderator3, 286) < 0.01,
  rel_dev(end_of(s_pulse)$Cc, 155) < 0.01
)

dplyr::bind_rows(
  transform(s_bolus, perturbation = "Cytokine bolus (2x baseline)"),
  transform(s_pulse, perturbation = "1 h ETX pulse, 4000 EU/kg/h")
) |>
  dplyr::select(time, perturbation, tnf, il6, moderator3) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(tnf, il6, moderator3), names_to = "state",
                      values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = perturbation)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~state, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Value (ng/L; EC50 in EU/L)",
       title = "Perturbation recovery to baseline", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Mass-balance / flux check

At the undisturbed baseline every turnover state has production equal to
elimination, so `d/dt = 0`. Verify symbolically for TNF-alpha and IL-6 using the
typical values.

```{r mass-balance}
rbase_tnf <- 281; mtt_tnf <- 1.04
kout_tnf <- 1 / mtt_tnf
kin_tnf <- rbase_tnf * kout_tnf
# With no ETX: eff_tnf = 0, so d/dt(tnf) = kin_tnf - kout_tnf * rbase_tnf.
stopifnot(abs(kin_tnf - kout_tnf * rbase_tnf) < 1e-9)

rbase_il6 <- 49.2; mtt_il6 <- 1.45
kout_il6 <- 5 / mtt_il6
kin_il6 <- rbase_il6 * kout_il6
# Each IL-6 chain stage flows at kout_il6 * rbase_il6 in and out at baseline.
stopifnot(abs(kin_il6 - kout_il6 * rbase_il6) < 1e-9)

# EC50 chain: kin_tol = EC0 * kout_tol, so the chain holds at EC0 with no ETX.
ec0 <- 286; mtt_tol <- 6.33
kout_tol <- 3 / mtt_tol
kin_tol <- ec0 * kout_tol
stopifnot(abs(kin_tol - kout_tol * ec0) < 1e-9)
c(kin_tnf = kin_tnf, kin_il6 = kin_il6, kin_tol = kin_tol)
```

# Replicate Figure 6

Figure 6 shows typical-value 30 h predictions of ETX (A), TNF-alpha (B), IL-6
(C) and the potency parameter EC50 (D) across initial infusion rates of 63, 250,
500, 1000, 4000, 8000 and 16000 EU/kg/h, with the four lowest rates switched to
4000 EU/kg/h after 15 h to demonstrate tolerance (an infusion dataset uses EU,
so the per-kg rate times the 27 kg mean weight gives the EU/h infusion). The
model has no weight covariate; the per-kg scaling is applied when the event
table is built. Each infusion goes to both ETX compartments.

```{r figure-6-sim}
wt <- 27 # mean piglet weight (kg), Thorsted 2019 Methods
rates <- c(63, 250, 500, 1000, 4000, 8000, 16000)

make_subject <- function(i, r) {
  switched <- r < 4000
  seg <- if (switched) {
    data.frame(time = c(0, 15), rate = c(r, 4000) * wt, dur = c(15, 15))
  } else {
    data.frame(time = 0, rate = r * wt, dur = 30)
  }
  seg$amt <- seg$rate * seg$dur
  dose <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    transform(seg, cmt = "central"),
    transform(seg, cmt = "central_contam")
  )
  dose <- dose[, c("time", "amt", "rate", "cmt")]
  dose$evid <- 1L
  obs <- data.frame(time = seq(0, 30, by = 0.25), amt = 0, rate = 0,
                    cmt = "tnf", evid = 0L)
  out <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs)
  out$id <- i
  out$rate_lab <- r
  out[order(out$time, -out$evid), ]
}

ev6 <- dplyr::bind_rows(Map(make_subject, seq_along(rates), rates))
for (nm in names(cov0)) ev6[[nm]] <- cov0[[nm]]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev6[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim6 <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ, ev6, keep = "rate_lab",
                        returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(rate_lab = factor(rate_lab, levels = rates))
```

```{r figure-6-plot, fig.height = 7}
sim6 |>
  dplyr::transmute(time, rate_lab,
                   `A: ETX (EU/L)` = Cc,
                   `B: TNF-alpha (ng/L)` = tnf,
                   `C: IL-6 (ng/L)` = il6,
                   `D: EC50 (EU/L)` = moderator3) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(time, rate_lab), names_to = "panel",
                      values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::filter(value > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = rate_lab)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = NULL, colour = "Initial rate\n(EU/kg/h)",
       title = "Figure 6 - typical-value 30 h predictions",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Thorsted 2019.")
```

The simulation reproduces the paper's Figure 6 behaviour:

```{r figure-6-checks}
summ <- sim6 |>
  dplyr::group_by(rate_lab) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    etx_plateau = Cc[time == 6],
    tnf_peak = max(tnf),
    tnf_tpeak = time[which.max(tnf)],
    tnf_second = max(tnf[time > 15]),
    il6_peak = max(il6),
    ec50_end = moderator3[time == 30],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
summ

stopifnot(
  # ETX plateau rises monotonically with infusion rate (Panel A).
  all(diff(summ$etx_plateau) > 0),
  # TNF-alpha peaks within the first few hours (Panel B).
  all(summ$tnf_tpeak <= 3),
  # TNF-alpha response increases with dose (Panel B).
  all(diff(summ$tnf_peak) > 0),
  # Tolerance (Discussion, on Fig 3A): a 4000 EU/kg/h challenge after
  # pre-exposure gives a response "much lower than without any pre-exposure",
  # and lower after the higher pre-exposure. Typical values, so deterministic.
  summ$tnf_second[summ$rate_lab == "63"] < 0.05 * summ$tnf_peak[summ$rate_lab == "4000"],
  summ$tnf_second[summ$rate_lab == "250"] < summ$tnf_second[summ$rate_lab == "63"],
  # EC50 climbs far above its EC0 = 286 baseline (tolerance; Panel D).
  all(summ$ec50_end > 1e4)
)
```

At a constant infusion rate `R` (EU/h) below `Vmax`, Michaelis-Menten
elimination has the closed-form steady state `C = KM * R / (Vmax - R)`, and the
tolerance chain then settles at `EC50 = EC0 * (1 + Tmax * C / (TC50 + C))`. The
4000 EU/kg/h arm (108000 EU/h) is effectively at steady state by 30 h, so its
simulated ETX and EC50 must match these values. A mis-transcribed `Vmax`, `KM`,
`Vc`, `EC0`, `Tmax` or `TC50` moves them by far more than the bound.

```{r figure-6-closed-form}
r_4000 <- 4000 * 27
c_ss <- 12600 * r_4000 / (442000 - r_4000)
ec50_ss <- 286 * (1 + 45100 * c_ss / (29300 + c_ss))
at30 <- sim6[sim6$rate_lab == "4000" & sim6$time == 30, ]
cf <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("ETX incl. baseline (EU/L)", "EC50 (EU/L)"),
  closed_form = c(155 + c_ss, ec50_ss),
  simulated = c(at30$Cc, at30$moderator3)
)
cf$rel_diff <- cf$simulated / cf$closed_form - 1
knitr::kable(cf, digits = c(0, 1, 1, 5),
             caption = "4000 EU/kg/h arm at 30 h vs. analytic steady state.")
# Measured residuals ~2e-4 (the chains are still converging); bound 10x above.
stopifnot(all(abs(cf$rel_diff) < 2e-3))
```

Reading Figure 6 by eye gives the same magnitudes: ETX plateaus near
4 x 10^3 EU/L at 4000 EU/kg/h and near 8 x 10^4 EU/L at 30 h for
16000 EU/kg/h (panel A); TNF-alpha peaks near 2 x 10^3 ng/L at 63 EU/kg/h and
2.4 x 10^5 ng/L at 16000 EU/kg/h (panel B); IL-6 settles near 2 x 10^3 ng/L
under 4000 EU/kg/h (panel C); and EC50 reaches about 1.5 x 10^6 EU/L at
4000 EU/kg/h and 9 x 10^6 EU/L at 16000 EU/kg/h (panel D). The figure's control
baselines sit at about 205 ng/L (TNF-alpha) and 49 ng/L (IL-6), the
EBE-median DuoSet baselines the paper used for study G, rather than the
study A/B typical values used here (281 and 49.2 ng/L). TNF-alpha production
scales with its baseline, so the TNF-alpha curves here sit about 1.4-fold
(281/205) above the figure's; solving with `lrbase_tnf = log(205)` and
`lrbase_il6 = log(49.3)` reproduces the figure's levels.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Structure from the control stream, values from Table 2.** The S1 Text
  `$THETA`/`$OMEGA` blocks hold the run045 initial estimates seeding the final
  importance-sampling run; the maintainers took every final value from Table 2,
  following the standard rule that a results table supersedes control-stream
  initials.
- **IIV variances read on the SD scale.** Table 2 reports variability as a
  CV% that equals `100 * sqrt(omega^2)` (footnote c, "approximate standard
  deviation scale"), so the variances encoded are `(CV/100)^2` and the KM-Vc
  covariance is `-0.42 * 1.20 * 0.753 = -0.3795`. The six fixed `$OMEGA`
  variances (0.000625) in the stream are structural parameters the paper did
  not vary and carry no IIV in the model.
- **Residual error is additive on log-transformed data**, which the maintainers
  encoded as `lnorm()` (Methods, "an additive relation was used for RUV
  (approximately proportional with log-transformed data)"); the BLOQ M3
  likelihood handling in the stream is an estimation detail with no bearing on
  simulation.
- **The mixture probability (0.399, fixed) is not an `ini()` parameter.**
  Following the `MIX_LARGE_BASE` precedent, it is documented in the
  `MIX_ETX_CONTAM` covariate entry; set the covariate to 0 for a typical
  uncontaminated animal or draw `Bernoulli(0.399)` per subject for a
  population.
- **No weight covariate.** The model reads no body weight; infusion rates are
  supplied in EU/h, so the per-kg rates of Figure 6 are multiplied by the 27 kg
  mean weight when the event table is built. Study G (external evaluation) is
  not part of the fit.
- **External-evaluation baselines.** For reproducing the held-out study G
  (Figure 5) the paper uses EBE-median baselines of 205 ng/L (TNF-alpha) and
  49.3 ng/L (IL-6); those are evaluation inputs, not model parameters, and are
  not encoded here.
- No correction notice was found for doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0211981 as of
  2026-10-16.
